basis: Congenital pituitary/thyroid hormone deficiency; neurodevelopmental delay and epiphyseal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%; hearing and optic abnormalities are occasional.
Motor-sensory axonal neuropathy; muscle wasting is secondary to denervation. Cardiomyopathy lacks evidence of a frequency reaching 30%.
Epidermolytic ichthyosis causes skin blistering, scaling, erosions and palmoplantar keratoderma.
Cholesterol synthesis defect with intellectual disability and characteristic syndactyly; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Ocular involvement omitted by cap; liver reports are sparse.
Congenital absence or severe hypoplasia of mitral valve leaflets causes mitral regurgitation.
Shoulder/thoracic skeletal deformities and congenital heart disease define the syndrome; thoracic malformation alone does not establish lung damage.
Permanent neonatal diabetes; intrinsic neurodevelopmental involvement is supported by global developmental delay in 4/13 patients (~31%).
Oesophagostomum helminth infection directly involves the intestinal tract.
Microphthalmia defines disease; callosal agenesis/developmental delay and cleft lip/palate each occur in the single reported patient (1/1); evidence is limited.
Congenital eyelid malformation with ectropion; exposure keratopathy remains within the ocular axis.
Brachydactyly is a digital skeletal malformation; anonychia is congenital absence of nails.
Seminoma arises in the reproductive testis; germ-cell origin does not establish endocrine disease. No other organ involvement is inherent.
Benign neoplasms arising in the liver or biliary system belong to the hepatic axis.
Dystroglycanopathies primarily cause muscular dystrophy; brain and eye damage varies across subtypes and is not established as common across this umbrella.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction; myopathic fibers 5/5 and weakness 3/5; hepatic steatosis 1/3. Atrial fibrillation 1/5 is below threshold.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability, autistic features and neurologic gait instability; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Characteristic cisplatin toxicity directly injures renal tubules, cochlear hair cells and peripheral axons; these are sites of the toxicity itself.
Malignant adipose tissue neoplasm arising in the ovary, a reproductive site outside the axes; histology does not establish skin or locomotor involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; cataracts 3/8 (~38%), hearing impairment 3/9 (~33%) and ventricular septal defects 3/9 (~33%) support involvement; cohorts are small.
Anemia is a red blood cell disorder, here with normal red cell volume; no additional organ damage is intrinsic.
Recurrent bacterial infection of hair follicles and surrounding skin, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus; associated immunodeficiency is a separate condition.
Tumor arises in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes; rhabdomyoblastic differentiation does not make it a skeletal muscle disease.
Germ cell malignancy arising in the reproductive testis; no intrinsic endocrine disorder or common direct involvement of another axis is established.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with ocular and skeletal myopathy. Cardiac findings in one patient do not establish common involvement; CNS/liver features are occasional (5-29%).
Developmental delay and ocular malformations are principal defining features; cardiac, pulmonary, skeletal and urogenital anomalies are variably reported without a common frequency.
